# Notes

## Base Diffusion Model

[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_diffusion_model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_diffusion_model)

![](data:image/png;base64,)
## Churn
- All services have a churn
- Watch out of Hell Levels where there is a difficulty bump compared the levels around it.

- Increased Churn for cohort hitting that level

## Level
- Number of encounters (or steps) to level is the real pace, rather than XP amount.
- Define level distances as a smooth ramp of number of successful encounters

- Pick a good looking cuve (1.2x e.g.)

- Walk through encounter logic to ensure steady feedback to the player via successful fights
- Fine tune by changing the number of encounters and cascading values back

- XP curve won’t change
- XP per monster will
- Player moment to moment pacing won’t

## Randomness
- Use cards instead of dice for randomization
- Much more predictable
- Multiple same dice can give a curve but there are still outliers
## Encounter Pacing

- What is the time delay between encounters?
- Curve set by

- Travel time
- Spawn rates
- Spawn frequency
## Rewards

- Bottom feeding is where you fight easier things because they have a higher ROI
- A form of twinking is tackling stuff higher than you should be able to
- The reward should then be bell curved
## Fun Fights

- One to one matches don’t have to be even. 90% of winning. Encourages ‘push your luck’.
- Watch all the curves!
- Monte Carlo modeling PVP
- Fun matches are tight
## Conclusions


- Model length of fight to calculate ‘time played between levels’
- Also ‘ammo needed per kill’

- Energy based systems - supply enough to leave the player just before a level up, or just past one - whatever tests better
- If you set a monetary value for energy or for ammo consumed per kill, you know the skipped playtime’s value
- Unpredictable advancement causes churn
- Fairly frequent rewards increase player engagement
- Tune reward pacing by

- Adjusting the size of the deck
- Number of kills per level
- Cost for a minute of advancement
- Etc
